basis: Cash basis; budget estimate as presented to Parliament, not outturn. Revenue for the same year is stated at TT$54,224mn, giving a deficit of TT$5,517mn (2.91% of GDP).
coverage: The Budget Statement itemises major allocations only. Named allocations cover TT$33,993mn of TT$59,741mn (56.9%); the balance is shown as a single residual and is NOT a published line item.
sourceDocument: Budget Statement 2025 — “Steadfast and Resolute: Forging Pathways to Prosperity”, delivered 30 September 2024

basis: Cash basis; approved estimates, not outturn. Non-debt recurrent J$769,900mn + capital J$80,000mn + public debt servicing J$491,200mn. Debt servicing is amortisation J$317,400mn plus interest J$173,800mn. TWO narrower denominators appear in the same document and are widely quoted: J$1,023,700mn (total expenditure excluding amortisation) and J$849,900mn (non-debt expenditure, the ministry table's own total). CaribEcon's fiscal series uses the J$1,023,700mn basis.
coverage: Exhaustive. Every portfolio ministry and department in the source table, plus public debt servicing. No residual and no estimation.
source: Jamaica Ministry of Finance & the Public Service
sourceDocument: The Citizens’ Guide to the 2024/2025 Budget
note: Listed components sum to J$1,341,200mn against a stated total of J$1,341,100mn — a J$100mn difference arising from the source's own rounding, which the table discloses as “(Slight Variation Due to Rounding of Numbers)”. Shares are computed against the sum of components so the segments total exactly 100%.
